summary.question: What is Crewola?
summary.answer: Crewola is a managed workflow service for home service companies, starting with HVAC, that turns service calls, quote requests and follow-ups into booked visits and clear handoffs, with your dispatchers and estimators in control. Every enquiry is captured and moved to a booked visit or a quote request, and pricing and dispatch always need human approval.
takeaways: Every enquiry is captured and moved to a booked visit or a quote request.
Diagnosis, safety decisions, binding quotes, discounts and dispatch commitments stay with qualified or authorised staff.
Pricing and dispatch always need human approval.
Results are measured by enquiries reaching a confirmed next step, compared with how you work today.

scope.covers: Heating, cooling and ventilation enquiries, plus plumbing, electrical and roofing where agreed, turned into visit requests, quote requests and follow-ups, for the teams and enquiry channels you choose.
scope.excludes: Diagnosis, safety decisions, repair instructions, binding quotes, discounts, dispatch commitments and live emergency response.
scope.instead: Those go to your dispatcher, estimator or duty contact. Urgent issues follow your business emergency protocol.

faq.a: HVAC first: heating, cooling and ventilation service calls, maintenance visits and replacement quotes. Plumbing, electrical and roofing enquiries can follow the same workflow. Each runs on your own service-area, scheduling and escalation rules.

faq.q: Will it produce a binding quote?
faq.a: No. Pricing always needs human approval. Only approved pricing can be shared within the agreed workflow; replacements, inspections and price exceptions go to your estimator.

faq.q: Can customers use this for emergencies?
faq.a: Not as an emergency service. Gas smells, carbon monoxide alarms and other urgent issues follow your business emergency protocol: Crewola flags them for your duty contact at once and sends only wording your team approved in advance. It gives no safety or repair instructions.

faq.q: Does it connect to our field-service software?
faq.a: Only where that is agreed after an assessment. We look at your current tools, permissions and integration options before agreeing scope, and no connection to a particular product is promised in advance.

workflow.heading: The next job starts with a clear brief.
workflow.intro: One task, start to finish: turning HVAC enquiries into booked visits, and where your dispatchers decide.
workflow.body: A homeowner calls while every technician is on a job. Someone has to take the details, check the service area and the schedule, and get the enquiry to the dispatcher. These are the eight steps from the first call to the closed record.

steps.title: The call comes in
steps.label: Request in
steps.body: A homeowner reports a heating or cooling problem through the website form, by phone or by message, on the channels your company chose. Every enquiry joins one shared list, including calls that came in while the crew was on a job.
steps.does: Reports a heating or cooling problem by web form, phone or message. It joins one shared list.

chat.text: Our AC is running but blowing warm air. Can someone come out tomorrow?

steps.title: Crewola reads it
steps.label: Sorted
steps.body: It works out the trade, the type of job and how urgent it is under your rules, and picks out the address, the equipment, the problem in the customer's own words and the preferred time.
steps.does: Sorts it by trade, job type and urgency, and picks out the address, equipment, symptom and preferred time.

chat.text: Sorted as an AC repair visit. Symptom: warm air. Time: tomorrow. Not urgent.

steps.title: Crewola checks the context
steps.label: Checked
steps.body: It checks your service area, the scheduling sources you allow and your dispatch rules. Equipment and visit history come from your field-service software only where that connection is agreed after an assessment.
steps.does: Checks the service area, schedule and dispatch rules you allow, and job history only where agreed.

chat.text: In service area. Two open windows tomorrow. No technician assigned yet.

steps.title: The homeowner hears back
steps.label: Reply drafted
steps.approval: Your team approves messages to customers before they go out.
steps.body: It drafts a reply with the expected response time from your rules. It does not diagnose the fault, quote a price or promise a technician or an arrival time.
steps.does: Drafts a reply with the response time from your rules. No diagnosis, price or arrival time.

chat.text: Thanks, Mark. Our dispatcher will confirm a visit window for tomorrow within 2 hours.
Approved. Send it.

steps.title: The dispatcher gets a full brief
steps.label: Handed off
steps.approval: Dispatchers and estimators decide prices, charges and technician assignments.
steps.body: The visit request goes to the dispatcher with everything they need. Prices, call-out charges, discounts and technician assignments are for the dispatcher or the estimator to decide.
steps.does: Briefs the dispatcher. Prices, charges, discounts and technician assignments stay with your team.

chat.text: Brief to Rosa: AC blowing warm air, tomorrow, Mark's number. Window and charge not set.

steps.title: Nothing is left waiting
steps.label: Chased
steps.body: The enquiry stays open against its expected time. If it slips, Crewola reminds the owner and then escalates to the person you name, such as the service manager.
steps.does: Keeps the enquiry open; reminds the owner if it slips, then escalates to the person you name.

chat.text: No visit confirmed after 1 hour. Reminder sent to Rosa.

steps.title: Dispatch books the visit
steps.label: Booked
steps.approval: Your team approves the confirmation to the customer before it is sent.
steps.body: The dispatcher assigns a technician and books the arrival window; a reply alone does not close an enquiry. Crewola then drafts the confirmation to the customer for your team to approve.
steps.does: The dispatcher assigns a technician and books the window; a reply alone does not close an enquiry.

chat.text: Booked Ken for tomorrow, 8 to 10 am.
You're booked for tomorrow, 8 to 10 am. Ken will call when he is on the way.

steps.title: Logged and reported
steps.label: Closed
steps.body: The enquiry is logged with who did what and when, and counted in regular reports on missed enquiries, time to a booked visit or quote handoff, and dispatcher effort.
steps.does: Logs who did what and when, and counts the enquiry in your regular reports.

chat.text: Logged: visit booked, each approver recorded. Enquiry closed.
